name: Downtown and Main Street
tagline: The brick main street, bars and the Ellen Theatre
description: Bozeman's historic centre along Main Street, with brick commercial buildings from the railroad era now holding the restaurants, breweries, outdoor shops and the Ellen Theatre. It is the one genuinely walkable part of the city and where most of the social life happens.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the bars, restaurants and shops on foot
pros: Restaurants, breweries and outdoor shops all walkable
The centre of the town's social life
Farmers market and events on the street
cons: The highest rents in the city

name: Montana State and the University District
tagline: South of downtown, students and the cheapest rooms
description: The area around Montana State University's campus, with student housing, cheap eating, the Museum of the Rockies and its dinosaur collection, and a young population. Rents here are the lowest close to the centre and the walk downtown takes about fifteen minutes.
bestFor: Budget stays close in, particularly during term
pros: The lowest rents within walking distance of downtown
Museum of the Rockies and campus facilities

name: Northeast Neighborhood
tagline: The old industrial quarter, now the interesting one
description: A small district northeast of downtown, historically railroad and industrial, now a mix of cottages, converted warehouses, a brewery and a few good restaurants. It has the most character of any residential area in Bozeman and a strong neighbourhood identity, five minutes from Main Street.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting character and a five-minute walk downtown
pros: Five minutes on foot to Main Street
Brewery and good restaurants within it

name: Bridger Canyon and the Ski Road
tagline: Out towards Bridger Bowl, in the mountains
description: The canyon road climbing northeast towards Bridger Bowl, the community-owned ski area twenty-five minutes from town, with scattered houses and cabins among the pines. It is the address for anyone whose winter is the reason they came, and the trailheads into the Bridgers start along it.
bestFor: Skiers and climbers who want the trailhead at the end of the drive
pros: Bridger Bowl and the range trailheads on the doorstep
cons: Twenty-five minutes into town, on a road that snows

name: Belgrade and the Valley
tagline: The valley towns, where the rents are survivable
description: The smaller towns spreading northwest down the Gallatin valley, Belgrade and Four Corners, where the airport sits and where housing costs a good deal less than in Bozeman itself. It is ordinary Montana valley living with the Bridgers on one side and the Spanish Peaks on the other.
bestFor: Longer stays priced out of Bozeman, with a car
pros: Same mountain access, shorter drive to Big Sky
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes into Bozeman
